DonationsFaq.whatIsEcolinkBody: A project developed to <bold>promote sustainability and the proper disposal of recyclable materials.</bold> The initiative seeks to facilitate conscious disposal by making materials deposited by UnB students available to recycling cooperative collectors.
DonationsFaq.whatAreEcopointsBody: They are the <bold>collection locations</bold> where recyclable materials can be dropped off. They can be found at various points on the Darcy Ribeiro Campus. Open the <bold>"Available Ecopoints"</bold> section and find the Ecopoint nearest to you!
DonationsFaq.howItWorksBody: To donate, you need a <bold>registered account with your student ID</bold> and an Ecopoint with available capacity. Scan the QR Code and follow the step-by-step instructions!
DonationsFaq.howToParticipateBody: At the beginning of each semester, the <bold>course "Ecolink Descarte que vale muito"</bold> is offered to students from all programs. To participate, simply enroll through SIGAA during the available enrollment period.
DonationsFaq.howToGetCreditsTitle: How do I earn credits by donating?
DonationsFaq.howToGetCreditsBody: To earn credits, the student must <bold>complete the required donations for the enrolled semester by the end of the term</bold>. You can check the previous screen to find out what the limit is.

EcopointFaq.title: How to know the Ecopoint status?
EcopointFaq.fullDescriptionPart1: The ecopoint in yellow means the bin is working correctly, but it is
EcopointFaq.fullDescriptionPart2: . It will be emptied soon and will be available for use again!
EcopointFaq.offlineDescriptionPart1: The ecopoint in gray means it is
EcopointFaq.offlineDescriptionPart2: with the system. In this case, the displayed status may not be up to date.
EcopointFaq.closedDescriptionPart1: The ecopoint in red means it is
EcopointFaq.closedDescriptionPart2: and is not available for donations at the moment.
